cards.title: Smaller than you think
cards.text: The Mona Lisa is only about 77 × 53 cm. Leonardo da Vinci worked on it for years and kept it with him until his death.

cards.title: Word maker
cards.text: Shakespeare's works contain the earliest recorded uses of many English words and phrases, such as 'eyeball', 'swagger' and 'wild-goose chase'.

cards.title: Composing in silence
cards.text: Beethoven was almost completely deaf when he composed his Ninth Symphony, first performed in 1824.

cards.question: Who painted 'The Starry Night'?
cards.explanation: He painted it in 1889 from his window at an asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence.

cards.question: Which novel introduced the phrase 'Big Brother is watching you'?
Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
A traditional haiku has how many syllables in total?

cards.statement: In Mary Shelley's novel, Frankenstein is the name of the monster.
cards.explanation: Victor Frankenstein is the scientist. The creature is never given a name.

cards.statement: Van Gogh is widely said to have sold only one painting in his lifetime.
cards.explanation: 'The Red Vineyard' is the only sale firmly documented, although he did trade and sell a few other works.

cards.statement: Sherlock Holmes says 'Elementary, my dear Watson' in Arthur Conan Doyle's stories.
cards.explanation: The exact phrase never appears in the original stories; it was popularised later by films.

cards.title: A first for film
cards.text: Toy Story (1995) was the first feature-length film made entirely with computer animation.

cards.question: Which city did the Beatles come from?

cards.statement: Tetris was created in the Soviet Union.
cards.explanation: Alexey Pajitnov created it in 1984 at the Soviet Academy of Sciences in Moscow.

cards.question: In chess, which piece can only move diagonally?
